newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal reaffirms it aims to join EMU from start.
newsitem.headline: Portugal reaffirms it aims to join EMU from start.

text.p: Portuguese Under-Secretary for Finance Fernando Teixeira dos Santos reiterated Portugal's commitment to join Economic and Monetary Union from the start.
"We want to enter (EMU in 1999) and we are determined that this should be possible," he told Reuters, reiterating the policy aim of the Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres.

He said remarks by a senior German official playing down expectations that Europe's single currency should begin with a big starting lineup, were "incomprehensible" as the Maastricht Treaty had set the terms for membership.

Juergen Stark, State Secretary at the Finance Ministry, said on Tuesday that some aspirants should foresake the political prestige of joining EMU at the outset. He said there were countries whose economic structures were not sufficiently prepared to take part.
He did not name names, but his comments appeared directed at so-called "Club Med" countries including Portugal that have not yet established a track record of exchange rate stability.
"I think the comments of Juergen Stark are incomprehensible because there is a Treaty which establishes membership requirements for the single currency," Teixeira dos Santos said.
